AnchorHealthResponse.description: Anchor lag, for the uptime check and the Phase 5 alarms (05 §3.6).
AnchorHealthResponse.title: AnchorHealthResponse

AnchorProofEntry.description: One audit row of this batch, and the proof for it if one exists yet.
AnchorProofEntry.title: AnchorProofEntry

AnchorTarget.description:
Where a Merkle root is published (04 §5.2).

The target is settled: OpenTimestamps to Bitcoin (05 §6.3). `polygon` is a
reserved fallback (06 §9) — the value exists so switching would not need a
migration; no code path in v2 consumes it.
AnchorTarget.title: AnchorTarget

BatchMetadataInput.description:
What the farmer declares about a batch at creation — the S0 pre-image.

`notes` is stored but deliberately outside the canonical payload, so fixing
a typo cannot invalidate anchored history (v1 Sprint 8; see
`stage_payloads.batch_metadata`). It is not shown on the anonymous
`/verify` view: free text is withheld there (`verification.FIELD_POLICY`).
BatchMetadataInput.title: BatchMetadataInput

ConformanceOut.description:
The Codex/KEBS verdict re-derived from the lab row now, under the rule
set recorded with it. Every limit and its basis travel with the result, so
a reader never needs to know which rules were in force.
ConformanceOut.title: ConformanceOut

ErrorResponse.description:
OpenAPI shape of the error envelope, so documented error responses match
what the handler emits (keeps the Schemathesis contract test honest).
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

HarvestRecordRequest.description:
S1. `harvest_date` is actor-asserted and hashed; an offset on the wire
is normalized to UTC before storage (see `models/types.UtcDateTime`).
HarvestRecordRequest.title: HarvestRecordRequest

HoneyType.description:
Validated here rather than as a PostgreSQL enum, so amending the list is
a one-file edit instead of an `ALTER TYPE` migration (v1 Sprint 8).
HoneyType.title: HoneyType

LabResultRequest.description:
S3. Every measurement names its quantity and its unit.

`02` R9 is why: v1 carried `sucrose_level`, which actually held total
sugars around 75-80% while the Codex sucrose limit is 5 g/100g, so a scorer
reading it would have failed every honest batch. Naming the field for what
it measures is the cheapest possible guard against that class of mistake.

Every parameter is optional. A lab that reports five of six should be able
to submit; the scorer marks the sixth `not_measured` and the verdict is
`INCOMPLETE` rather than a confident pass.
LabResultRequest.title: LabResultRequest

MetadataPublic.description:
The farmer's declaration as the anonymous `/verify` view shows it.

No `notes`: free text can carry personal data whatever it was meant for,
and this view is broadcast to anyone who scans a jar.
MetadataPublic.title: MetadataPublic

PackagingRecordRequest.description:
S4. One QR per batch, so v1's per-jar `qr_codes` is gone; `unit_count`
already equals the jar count.
PackagingRecordRequest.title: PackagingRecordRequest

PingResponse.description:
Minimal typed response so the OpenAPI schema has real content for the
generated TypeScript client to consume. Phase 1 replaces this with the
real domain schemas.
PingResponse.title: PingResponse

ProofStepOut.description: One sibling on the path to the root; `position` is the sibling's side.
ProofStepOut.title: ProofStepOut

StageRecordedResponse.description: What a transition returns: where the batch now is, and what it recorded.
StageRecordedResponse.title: StageRecordedResponse

StageVerificationOut.description:
One stage of the three-way match.

`payload` is the canonical pre-image as the stage row stands now. When
`payload_precision` is `exact`, hashing it reproduces `recomputed_hash`.
When it is `reduced`, the fields in `redacted_fields` were coarsened or
withheld for privacy and **both hashes are omitted**, because they commit
to the exact values; `match` is then the server's own comparison.
StageVerificationOut.title: StageVerificationOut

StageVerifications.description: `null` means the batch has not reached that stage yet.
StageVerifications.title: StageVerifications

info.description: Honey provenance and traceability: hash-chained audit log, Merkle anchoring via OpenTimestamps, PostGIS geospatial records.
info.title: ApiChain v2 Backend

get.description:
Anchor lag: how far the public witness trails the log (05 §3.6).

A separate endpoint rather than extra fields on /audit/health, so the
Phase 1 contract does not move. Phase 5's alarms read these fields.

post.description:
S4 -> S5. Terminal: `transitions` gives DISTRIBUTED no successor, so
every transition endpoint refuses a distributed batch, this one included.

S2 -> S3, and the only transition that produces a judgement.

A failing verdict does **not** block the transition: `LAB_VERIFIED` means a
lab result has been recorded, not that the honey passed. Conflating them
would make a failing result unrecordable, which is how bad results go
missing. The verdict is anchored and surfaced instead.

get.description:
Typed liveness probe under /v2. Exists to give the contract guardrails
a real typed endpoint to generate and consume; not a domain endpoint.

Everything needed to verify this batch's records offline.

One entry per audit row, each carrying its own status, so a record that
exists in our log but has no public anchor yet is reported as `pending`
rather than as a missing field (03 §6).

The three-way match over every recorded stage of this batch.

Being anonymous, it applies `verification.FIELD_POLICY` (hive coordinates
at 2 dp, altitude at 100 m, free text and the analyst's name withheld) and
publishes no hashes for a redacted block. Staff see exact values in an
authenticated view, never here. Reports facts only: no score, no band —
those mappings are the client's (03 §1, §6).
